Let R be the real line. Consider the following subsets of the plane R × R :
$ S$ = {(x, y) : y = x + 1 and 0 < x < 2}
$ T$ = {(x, y) : x – y is an integer}.

options: T is an equivalence relation on R but S is not
Neither S nor T is an equivalence relation on R
Both S and T are equivalence relations on R
S is an equivalence relation on R but T is not
questions.explanation:
**Explain Question : Compare two subsets of a plane to see which, if any, represent an equivalence relation on the real line.
$ $**Concept : Equivalence relations and the definition of the "Integers" set in coordinate geometry.
$ $**Solution :
$ We$ have : T = {(x, y) : x – y ∈ Z].
$ T$ is reflexive. [$\u$2235 (x, x) ∈ Z ⇒ (x – x) i.e. 0 ∈ Z]
$ T$ is symmetric.
$ [∵ (x, y) ∈ Z ⇒ x – y ∈ Z ⇒ y – x ∈ Z ⇒ (y, x) ∈ Z]$
$ T$ is transitive. [$\u$2235 (x, y) ∈ Z, (y, w) ∈ Z ⇒ (x – y) ∈ Z, y – w ∈ Z]
$ $⇒ (x – y) + (y – w) = (x – w) ∈ Z ⇒ (x, w) ∈ Z]
$ Thus$, T is an equivalence relation.
$ We$ have : S = {(x, y) : y = x + 1, 0 < x < 2}.
$ S$ is not reflexive.
$ [∵ (x, x) ∈ S ⇒ x = x + 1 ⇒ 0 = 1, which is impossible]$
$ Hence$ T is an equivalence relation and S is not .
$ $**Final Answer : **(A)
$ $
